head: 37c1fdf1566284e652a2a12cbda0334535ea783a
note: A new warehouse source (Cloudflare R2 Data Catalog, Iceberg REST). Golden issues are the union of the real findings that other review bots posted on this commit or the next one. Each issue was present at the head commit.

issues.summary: Vended R2 storage credentials (s3.secret-access-key, s3.session-token) in loadTable responses reach HTTP sample capture: the catalog session keeps capture on and redacts only the API token; the scrubber's REDACT_FIELD_NAMES misses those keys.

When the saved resume snapshot expires after some full-refresh batches loaded, extraction restarts from the new snapshot while the pipeline resume state is still valid, so the loaded prefix is kept and the replay appends to it: duplicated and stale rows.
Iceberg identifier fields are advertised as primary keys for incremental merge without a uniqueness check; Iceberg does not enforce uniqueness, so dedupe on merge silently drops distinct rows.
Schema alignment is not recursive: nested struct/list/map children that were renamed or deleted keep their old names or fields, so rows do not match the current Iceberg schema.
Parquet files without field IDs are resolved by current column name only, ignoring the table's schema.name-mapping.default, so a renamed column reads as null.

Columns absent from a data file are filled with null instead of identity-partition values from the manifest or the field's initial-default; this corrupts data and drops rows when the column is the cursor.
A bare @dataclasses.dataclass (resume state) breaks the repository invariant test test_no_new_undeclared_dataclasses / the code-style rule to declare frozen; CI fails.
Position delete files are loaded whole and every file's deleted positions are kept in memory before any data is read; memory grows with total deletes, independent of batch size or pruning.
Splitting a position delete file by target data file runs pc.equal + filter over all records once per target: O(records x targets).
Every 5,000-row batch calls pc.is_in against the full deleted-positions array, rebuilding the lookup each batch: O(batches x deletes).

open_file / read_bytes download whole objects with no total size limit, deadline or shutdown check (spooling only moves the bytes to disk); slow or huge source-controlled files exhaust disk/memory or never stop.
get_schemas loads every discovered table's metadata serially from a synchronous request path; large catalogs make setup and schema refresh slow enough to hit request deadlines.
A removed or retyped incremental cursor column raises an error that get_non_retryable_errors does not match, so scheduled syncs retry a permanent failure.

account_id and bucket_name pick which catalog the stored token is used against but are not in the retarget-guarded fields (only catalog_uri) nor in credential_identity_fields, so a member can change the bucket/account and keep the stored token, and a shared credential row is retargeted as a rotation.

The Cloudflare host allowlist check accepts a URL with a backslash in the authority (https://attacker.example\catalog.cloudflarestorage.com/...), which requests/urllib3 sends to attacker.example with the bearer token.

Discovery walks the whole namespace tree and every list_tables page before applying the table cap, and validate_credentials does the full walk synchronously in source setup; unbounded work driven by the catalog.

Manifest planning ignores DELETED manifest entries: after a compaction or overwrite, the removed file stays ADDED in an inherited manifest and the DELETED entry in the new manifest is its only removal record, so the sync reads deleted files and duplicates or keeps stale rows.
get_schemas(names=...) filters after the discovery cap, so a stored table beyond the cap is not found.
